title: performance(canary): enhanced auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Our perf canary pipeline detects regressions by comparing recent runs to a rolling baseline, but it has been noisy for short-lived spikes and missed multi-metric regressions (latency + throughput). This PR improves automated detection heuristics, adds adaptive thresholds and cohort-aware baselines, and introduces rollout guards that block or rollback deployments when the canary crosses multi-dimensional SLO regressions. Summary of changes: - Add multi-metric detection engine that reasons jointly about p95 latency, p99 latency, and tokens/s (throughput) with covariance-aware thresholds. - Implement cohort-aware baselining: separate baselines for production traffic shapes (short vs long sequences, batching levels). - Adaptive thresholding: thresholds adjust based on baseline volatility (using EWMA of variance) to reduce false positives from transient noise. - Rollout guards: declarative config that can block canary->stable promotion, trigger automatic rollback, or reduce traffic percentage when combined metrics breach thresholds. - Observability: new perf_canary_summary and perf_canary_alert metrics, dashboards and a condensed alert payload to reduce noise in PagerDuty. - Tests and CI: deterministic unit tests for detector; integration tests with perf-canary lab that mock traffic shapes. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4321) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Metrics + dashboards updated - [x] Backwards-compatible config for existing rollout policies - [x] QA ran perf canary lab runs for 3 representative models Notes: the description below includes the implementation summary and rationale for reviewers. Please focus review on detector thresholds, the cohort definition heuristics, and the rollout guard API surface.

review_comments: Jordan Li: The EWMA window defaults look aggressive; can we make them configurable per-cohort?
Asha Patel (author): Made the EWMA window configurable and added tests for edge cases in test_multi_metric_detector.py
Maya Singh: We need to ensure alerts won't flood PD for high-frequency canaries; can the condensed payload be rate-limited?
Asha Patel: Condensed payload + grouping logic added; integration test shows PD noise reduced by ~90% in lab runs.
Owen Brooks: The rollout_guard API looks good but do we have an escape hatch for emergency ship? Suggest admin override flag in the rollout controller.
Asha Patel: Added 'force_promote' operator action gated by RBAC and audit log entry; also added an integration test for audit logging.
approvals: Maya Singh: approved with minor comments addressed
release_notes: Improved perf canary detection: multi-metric (p95/p99/throughput) detectors, cohort-aware baselines, adaptive thresholds and rollout guards. Adds new metrics perf_canary_summary and perf_canary_alert, dashboards, and a guard API to block/rollback promotions. Backwards-compatible config.
incident_context: This change was prompted by a recent false-negative on a canary that degraded throughput while p95 remained stable (SUP-2123). The new detector found a joint regression pattern in lab replay.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for detector math and edge cases. Integration tests use perf-canary lab to replay short/long sequence cohorts and validate guard actions. CI run flaked on the first e2e-perf run (timeout), retried and passed.
notes_for_ops: Operators: rollout guard config is under api/rollouts/schema.yaml. Default behavior is to block promotion on multi-metric breach. To change, update Helm chart deploy/helm/perf-canary-values.yaml and redeploy the rollout-controller. Emergency promote requires 'force_promote' RBAC permission.
